issues.description: The problem statement (UML and description) requires a static method named calculateTotalPrice(Meal): int, but both the provided code and the reference solution use a method named computeMealCost(Meal). This name/signature mismatch between the specification and the codebase can confuse students about which method to implement and what tests will expect.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across the problem statement, template, and solution. Preferably update the code to implement the method name used in the specification (calculateTotalPrice) or change the problem text/UML to reference computeMealCost everywhere. Also update example usages in Main accordingly so students and tests target the same method name.

issues.description: The problem text instructs that the SealSaloon should have a final Stock stock and that this should be initialized in the SealSaloon constructor. Later the statement requires that the stock attribute must be static (shared across instances). Initializing a static final field in an instance constructor is incorrect in Java and will confuse students: static final fields must be assigned at declaration or in a static initializer, not in the instance constructor. The reference solution declares stock as a static final field and initializes it at declaration (not in the constructor), resolving the conflict, but the instructions in the problem are contradictory.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the specification: explicitly state that stock is a static (class-level) field and should be initialized at its declaration or in a static initializer, not in the instance constructor. Alternatively, if the intention is instance-level stock, remove the 'static' requirement from the note. Update the problem text to remove the contradictory instruction to initialize stock in the SealSaloon constructor.

issues.description: The problem statement requires a static method named calculateTotalPrice(Meal) to compute a meal's total price, but both the provided template comment and the solution implementation use the name computeMealCost(Meal). This mismatch means students reading the problem will look for or attempt to implement calculateTotalPrice while the codebase (and example usage in Main) expects computeMealCost, creating confusion mapping the requirement to the actual method to call/implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across artifacts. Either (A) rename computeMealCost(Meal) to calculateTotalPrice(Meal) in the solution and update all references (e.g., Main), or (B) update the problem statement to refer to computeMealCost(Meal). Ensure the template, solution, and problem statement use the same identifier so students can unambiguously map requirement to implementation.
